entries.subject: Selected model
entries.finding: [Selected model](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/146) and [original counted mesh](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/stored_files/open/319/shape.txt) — included unchanged. Convex light-curve inversion; fine relief is unresolved.

entries.subject: DAMIT documentation
entries.finding: [DAMIT documentation](https://damit.cuni.cz/pages/documentation) — coordinate units, pole, period and diameter semantics. CC BY 4.0.

entries.subject: J. Ďurech et al. (2009), Asteroid models from combined sparse and dense photometric data
entries.finding: [J. Ďurech et al. (2009), Asteroid models from combined sparse and dense photometric data](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009A%26A...493..291A) — original model publication record.

entries.subject: Hanuš (2011), A study of asteroid pole-latitude distribution based on an extended set of shape models derived by the lightcurve inversion method
entries.finding: [Hanuš (2011), A study of asteroid pole-latitude distribution based on an extended set of shape models derived by the lightcurve inversion method](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011A%26A...530A.134H) — original model publication record.

entries.subject: AKARI AcuA
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — excluded from physical scaling because the shape-aware VS-TPM fit is available. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 64.01 ± 0.73 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented.
entries.revisitWhen: New evidence invalidates the selected shape-aware thermal fit or establishes that an effective-sphere diameter is the appropriate physical scale.

entries.subject: Hanuš et al. 2017
entries.finding: [Hanuš et al. 2017](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.01996), [Viikinkoski et al. 2017](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.05191), and [Vernazza et al. 2021](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/references/view/660) — resolved-model releases surveyed; when present in this target’s archive they are preferred over an older convex model. Their disk images constrain geometry but are not registered global reflectance mosaics.

entries.subject: Hanuš et al. 2018
entries.finding: [Hanuš et al. 2018](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.06116) and [occultation dimensions](https://www.asteroidoccultation.com/observations/Asteroid_Dimensions_from_Occultations.html) — VS-TPM selected for this pole family; occultation ellipsoids are not silently substituted for mesh volume.

entries.subject: Registered surface imagery
entries.finding: The release supplies no registered surface imagery; the grid marks that gap.
entries.revisitWhen: A released, reusable surface observation or mapped product with registration to this body’s selected source model; the existing grid alone does not imply that every archive was searched.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Only a uniform scale from the published thermophysical fit is transferred to the archived nominal mesh. The varied-model ensemble does not establish identical mesh bytes or local surface accuracy. The alternative pole remains possible. No thermal or reflectance map is inferred. Alternative archive solutions: model 147, pole ['349', '-33'], [Model 147](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/147)
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.
